contexts.text: The things which are of service, or which serve, are relatively servants, and are called servants.
The delight of being of service to others; thus wanting to be the least.
By dignities (a spiritual man) can be of service to the neighbour...
When the things of the external man... are of service to the ends of the internal.
For the use of being inservient to heavenly delight.
(Wealth, food, etc.) held as a means of subserving the end.
Truth which is of service for introducing genuine goods and truths. AC 3993:7.
When it has subserved this purpose...
They had subserved only as means.
When the Natural ministers to and subserves the Rational.
When sensuous things minister to or subserve interior ones.
That they may subserve the interior Natural. Signified, Explained.
Exteriors ought to subserve interiors.
Everyone there wants to minister to and be of service to another.
They do not think of eminence, but only about being of service.
Into the scientifics serviceable to them. Signified, Explained.
The choice of inservient truths. Signified, Explained.

The external of man ought to be inservient to the internal... As the world ought to serve Heaven, so the external of man ought [to serve] his internal... (Thus) the external of man is not anything unless it is inservient to the internal, and it is something so far as it is inservient. To be inservient is to obey. Explained.
(These infernals) are sometimes taken out, that they may be of service to others for some uses which are vile.
A servant properly = one who is of service, or one who, or that which, is of service.
The will of being of service. Signified, Explained.
They subserve the former as receptacles.
The priesthood is inservient only.
The affection of fructifying is in man when he loves to be of service.
He regards himself as the highest in order of those who are of service to others.
